title: Getty Images v. Stability AI tests whether generative AI training on scraped images infringes copyright
description: Getty Images sued Stability AI in the UK High Court in January 2023, alleging that millions of its copyrighted images were used without a license to train the Stable Diffusion generative image model, alongside separate trademark and database-right claims. Getty dropped its primary training/scraping-based copyright claim during trial, reportedly for jurisdictional and evidentiary reasons. On 4 November 2025, the High Court rejected Getty's remaining secondary copyright infringement claim and its broader trademark claim, finding only limited trademark infringement tied to early Stable Diffusion outputs that reproduced a Getty watermark, and awarded no finding of copyright infringement.

history.note: Initial Phase 2A seed content, part of the Foundational Twenty. The 'millions of images' figure is as alleged by Getty in pleadings, not a court-established fact. Whether the judgment is under appeal was not confirmed at time of writing; treat 'final' status as unconfirmed.

Normalized US/UK spelling variants to the American-English house style (schema field names, e.g. organizations_involved, are already American; majority framework citations - NIST, FTC, EEOC, FCRA, BIPA - are American sources).

root_cause: Alleged unlicensed use of copyrighted training images scraped from the internet to train a commercial generative AI model, combined with unresolved legal questions about whether AI model training constitutes copyright infringement under UK law and whether the training activity occurred within UK jurisdiction.

citations.title: Getty Images (US) Inc and others v Stability AI Limited [2025] EWHC 2863 (Ch)
citations.publisher: Courts and Tribunals Judiciary (England and Wales High Court)

relationships.reason: A requirement to document training-data provenance and licensing review before commercial deployment addresses the underlying governance gap this litigation exposed.
This is the most closely watched generative-AI training-data litigation to reach a first-instance judgment.
